chunks: ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:

There is no man who withholds a dirham from its rightful due except that he will spend two in other than its rightful due. And there is no man who withholds a rightful due in his wealth except that Allah will collar him with it as a serpent of fire on the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.حَقًّا: an obligatory right owed from one's wealth
key_terms.حَقِّهِ: its rightful due or proper claim
key_terms.حَيَّةً: a serpent; here, a form of punishment
key_terms.دِرْهَمًا: a unit of money; here, even a small withheld amount
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection, when final judgment occurs

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say about withholding the rightful dues of wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith warns against withholding the rightful dues attached to wealth, such as zakat and similar financial obligations. It teaches that refusing to give what is due brings loss in this world and punishment in the Hereafter. The narration joins financial duty with moral accountability before Allah.
